explanation: L2/N1511+ triggers on a subword fragment: it fires while the model is spelling a word out of pieces rather than emitting a whole word, peaking on the short piece that OPENS a multi-piece word in non-English text (Italian 'nu' of nuovo and 'cons'+'ig' of consiglio, French 'qu'+'’' of qu'une, Spanish 'pr' of pronto, Greek 'δ' of βραδινές, Cyrillic 'в' of подвижной) and decaying across the word's remaining pieces to ~0 on the piece that completes it (mean activation 0.42 / 0.23 / 0.02, on a max of 3.60, at first / middle / last piece of a held-out multilingual set). Whole-word tokens stay at or just above the 0.22 first-position floor, so plain English and German prose peaks at 0.2-1.0 (0.06-0.28 x max, around the 0.25 x max active line of 0.90) while Italian, French, Spanish, Greek, Russian and Indic prose peaks at 1.6-3.5 (0.45-0.97 x max; 0.24% of scanned English tokens active versus 1.5% German and 10-12% Hindi, Bengali, Tamil and Greek), and its write boosts the next piece of the word being spelled (zero-ablating the pole drops 'ovo' by 0.26 and 'end' by 0.11; lookahead stays at KL 0.010, is_lookahead False; the negative pole is pinned to GELU's floor, max 0.17, and carries no signal).
